newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks stumble off month lows at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks stumble off month lows at open.

text.p: The Australian share market climbed off its month lows on Wednesday in light early trading after Wall Street closed higher.
The All Ordinaries index added 6.8 points to 2,644.4.

Early trade was choppy, although most of leaders posted modest gains on generally light turnover. Brokers said the gains were likely to be minor, with a short-term trading horizon likely to be focussing traders' attention.
"I think people will be buying and selling to try and take advantage of small margins as they appear," said Melbourne-based Peake Lands Kirwan broker, Kevin Lourey.
Among individual stocks, gold miner Great Central Mines Ltd added 27.8 cents to a high of A$2.738 (USS2.00) amid rumours of a bid from Canadian giant Barrick Gold Corp.
Traders said a lot more of such talk could be expected given the weak state of the gold price which was leaving plenty of the lower cost producers vulnerable to takeover.
"You will find a lot of those rumours start to surface now obviously because of the gold price," said Peter Saunders of Perth brokerage D.J. Carmichael and Co.
Elsewhere, it was a mixed performance with few standouts.
